progress-calendar-ahead-04.text: Choose what genuinely needs to happen, then move or remove something that can wait. Leave space between commitments.

progress-calendar-ahead-08.text: Add a little preparation and journey time around the appointment. A calendar is more useful when it includes getting there.

progress-calendar-ahead-06.text: That requires your actual calendar entries. Review the coming evenings and include commitments that may not be recorded.

progress-calendar-ahead-07.text: Create and verify a reminder in a calendar or alarm service that supports notifications. A saved Daywell plan alone may not notify you.

progress-calendar-ahead-09.text: Find the planned run on tomorrow's date and confirm it is the right entry before removing it.

progress-calendar-behind-01.text: Open your history for the month and review the movement entries. Remember that unlogged activity will not appear there.

progress-calendar-ahead-10.text: Yes. Leave space for sleep, meals, movement you want, and rest. Your calendar can reflect care as well as commitments.

progress-calendar-behind-03.text: You can make a dated entry for yesterday where the app supports it. Check the date before saving.

progress-calendar-behind-02.text: That needs your saved history and what rest means to you. Look back for a day with room to recover.

progress-calendar-behind-04.text: Look for the earliest movement entry in your history. You can add a reflection about what that beginning meant to you.

progress-calendar-behind-05.text: It may not have been logged, or it may be under another date. Check the records before assuming it was lost.

progress-calendar-behind-06.text: No. A calendar shows recorded plans and entries. It cannot measure your effort or everything that mattered that day.

progress-calendar-behind-07.text: Choose one meaningful change, such as an easier routine or asking for help sooner. Progress does not have to be a number.

progress-calendar-behind-08.text: Open the correct task and update its status. Check the date and details so your history remains accurate.

progress-calendar-behind-09.text: Find the entry in your history and edit the details available there. Review it after saving to confirm the correction.

progress-calendar-behind-10.text: A short journal note can capture the experience around a day. Useful history can include how things felt, not only what got done.

progress-calendar-connections-03.text: A calendar file export is a snapshot. Changes in another calendar do not automatically update Daywell.

progress-calendar-connections-02.text: You can use the calendar export file with a compatible calendar app. Check the imported dates and times after adding it.

progress-calendar-connections-01.text: Daywell currently offers calendar file export, rather than live Google Calendar synchronisation. Check the export options in the calendar.

progress-calendar-connections-04.text: Use the calendar export control, then check the dates included in the file before importing it elsewhere.

progress-calendar-connections-05.text: The receiving calendar may contain duplicates. Review those entries there before removing anything you want to keep.

progress-calendar-connections-06.text: A prepared reply cannot access your Google events. Daywell's file export does not grant access to that calendar.

progress-calendar-connections-09.text: You can use Daywell's own calendar and history. Connecting another calendar is not required to keep a record.

progress-calendar-connections-08.text: An export can contain personal plans. Review its contents and share it only with someone you intend to receive those details.

progress-calendar-connections-07.text: Check the time zone and event details in both places. Correct the event only after confirming which time you intended.

progress-appointment-preparation-01.text: Check the time, place, and what you need to bring. Keep those details in one place you can find easily.

progress-appointment-preparation-02.text: Write down your main concern, how long it has been happening, and any questions you do not want to forget.

progress-calendar-connections-10.text: Choose which calendar you will check regularly. With file exports, review changes carefully because the copies do not stay in sync.

progress-appointment-preparation-03.text: The calendar needs the date, time, and details you want saved. Review the entry before confirming it.

progress-appointment-preparation-05.text: You can take notes and ask for clarification or written instructions. Bring a trusted person if that is appropriate and you want support.

progress-appointment-preparation-04.text: Work backwards from arrival time and include getting ready. A separate leaving reminder may be more useful than the appointment time alone.

progress-appointment-preparation-07.text: Check how to contact the organiser and ask about the next available option. Update your calendar once the new time is confirmed.

progress-appointment-preparation-08.text: Leave a small gap after it if you can. A short pause can give you room before the next commitment.

progress-appointment-preparation-10.text: That needs your saved notes. Open the relevant entry and check the questions you recorded.

progress-appointment-preparation-09.text: Contact the provider or organiser to find out the next step. Then update your plans with the confirmed information.

progress-setbacks-context-01.text: A difficult week does not erase earlier helpful moments. Consider what changed, and seek support if you are struggling to cope.

progress-setbacks-context-02.text: Look at the circumstances around the change. You may need a different amount of support or a smaller plan right now.

progress-setbacks-context-04.text: One difficult period does not make the good week unreal. Keep the useful parts and adjust what no longer fits.

progress-setbacks-context-06.text: Their circumstances and starting points may be different. Choose a change that is meaningful in your own life.

progress-setbacks-context-05.text: A record is information, not a grade. Ask what would make the next few days more manageable.

progress-setbacks-context-07.text: You can pause reviewing it and think about what information is useful to keep. Check what deletion removes before making that choice.

progress-setbacks-context-09.text: Habits are not a substitute for the support you may need. Consider speaking with a qualified professional or someone you trust.

progress-setbacks-context-08.text: An app can offer tools and small supports, but change can take time and outside help. You do not have to do it all here.

progress-setbacks-context-10.text: Choose something that fits the next day, not your most ambitious week. A manageable step can give you a place to return.

progress-long-view-02.text: A manageable movement routine may support that aim. Get appropriate guidance for your health and abilities as you build it.

progress-long-view-01.text: Daywell cannot promise a longer life. It can support everyday routines around movement, food, rest, and sleep.

progress-long-view-03.text: Choose a version that fits ordinary, busy weeks. A flexible routine is easier to return to when life changes.

progress-long-view-05.text: Focus on activities and routines that matter to you. A score cannot capture your whole health or your life.

progress-long-view-04.text: You do not need to turn life into constant measurement. Choose a few supports that leave room for enjoyment and rest.

progress-long-view-08.text: Let the routine remove friction. Choose fewer steps and make room for days when only the basics happen.

progress-long-view-09.text: Notice whether it makes useful actions easier or gives you a welcome pause. You can keep what helps and drop what does not.

progress-long-view-07.text: Try an intention about how you want daily life to feel, such as having more room for rest or easier access to movement.

everyday-say-hello-01.text: Hello. You can arrive just as you are. What would make this moment a little easier?

everyday-say-hello-02.text: Welcome back. You can put the day down for a moment. A quiet pause is a good enough place to start.

progress-long-view-10.text: Yes. Your priorities can change with your circumstances. Choose a definition that supports the life you are living now.

everyday-say-hello-05.text: Hello there. Let this be one undemanding moment in the middle of your day.

everyday-say-hello-03.text: You do not need a clear reason. You can take a small pause and see what, if anything, would help.

everyday-say-hello-04.text: There is no task you have to complete. You can listen, use a tool, or simply leave when you are ready.

everyday-say-hello-06.text: You can keep the details to yourself. Choose a quiet recording if listening feels easier than talking.

everyday-say-hello-07.text: You can say what you need in ordinary words, such as help me unwind, or I want to move a little.

everyday-say-hello-08.text: Start with one small need. You can explore a guided moment or a simple tool without setting up your whole life.

everyday-say-hello-10.text: Ordinary days belong here too. You can make room for a small comfort without waiting for a difficult moment.

everyday-one-host-01.text: No. You can ask Daywell in your own words. The companions are there to make the experience feel welcoming.

everyday-say-hello-09.text: Yes. A few quiet minutes can be a complete visit. You do not need to turn them into a goal.

everyday-one-host-02.text: Just ask Daywell for a gentle sleep or wind down moment. You do not need to call a separate companion.

everyday-one-host-03.text: Luma accompanies quiet moments, rest, and settling down. You can simply choose the kind of support you want.

everyday-one-host-04.text: Bounce brings friendly company to movement. You can ask Daywell about moving without remembering a special command.

everyday-one-host-06.text: They bring a little company to food and everyday care. You do not need to manage them or give them separate instructions.

everyday-one-host-07.text: No. The companions do not need feeding, attention, or a daily visit. They are here to support your experience.

everyday-one-host-05.text: Pip accompanies focus and manageable next steps. The task can stay small, even when your thoughts feel busy.

everyday-one-host-09.text: That is the idea: use ordinary words with Daywell. You do not need to choose a different assistant for every need.

everyday-one-host-08.text: No companion is keeping score or waiting for an explanation. You can return whenever the app is useful.

everyday-one-host-10.text: The companions are illustrated characters, and the voices are AI generated. They do not have human experiences or feelings.

everyday-audio-controls-03.text: Use the stop or pause control when you want quiet. You are free to end the audio at any time.

everyday-audio-controls-02.text: Use the voice volume control in the session or your device volume. This saved reply cannot change that setting.

everyday-audio-controls-01.text: In the new unwind sessions, choose a voice and use its preview button. The full session begins only when you press begin.

everyday-audio-controls-06.text: Yes. Just listen contains prerecorded moments. Those recordings do not need microphone access.

everyday-audio-controls-05.text: Headphones are optional. Use a comfortable listening setup and volume, in a place where it is safe to settle.

everyday-audio-controls-04.text: Use the session position control to move back, or replay a short recording. Choose only as much as you want to hear.

everyday-audio-controls-08.text: The guidance is available as text. Open the full guidance if you would like to follow the session in writing.

everyday-audio-controls-07.text: Selecting an unwind voice does not start audio. Use preview or begin when you are ready to listen.

everyday-audio-controls-09.text: Use these settling exercises after you have arrived safely. Do not follow relaxation or breathing cues while driving.

everyday-privacy-choices-01.text: Prerecorded listening does not require the microphone. Check the separate live voice control if you have started a conversation.

everyday-audio-controls-10.text: These saved recordings are in English. Other languages would need supported, separately prepared guidance or a live conversation.

everyday-privacy-choices-02.text: Live voice uses ElevenLabs after you choose to connect. Review the consent and privacy information before starting.

everyday-privacy-choices-04.text: Data deletion needs the appropriate account or data controls. A prerecorded reply cannot delete stored information.

everyday-privacy-choices-05.text: That depends on the device and account session. Use appropriate device protection and check your sign in state when sharing a device.

everyday-privacy-choices-03.text: Keep passwords, payment details, and private security codes out of conversations. They are not needed for a calming moment.

everyday-privacy-choices-07.text: Yes. You can say you had a difficult day without naming people or sharing private information.

everyday-privacy-choices-08.text: Use the privacy information provided for the app and its voice service. A saved reply may not reflect later changes to those terms.

everyday-privacy-choices-06.text: Daywell's live voice setup does not automatically include your journal. What you choose to say in a conversation is still shared with the voice service.

everyday-comfort-preferences-01.text: Use the gentle movement control to turn animation off. You can keep the companion still while you listen.

everyday-privacy-choices-10.text: End the live conversation if you want to stop sharing. Check the service's data controls or support options for any stored information.

everyday-privacy-choices-09.text: I cannot make that promise. Check how the app and its voice provider process data before sharing sensitive information.

everyday-comfort-preferences-03.text: Keep them open. You can rest your gaze somewhere ordinary and stay aware of the room.

everyday-comfort-preferences-04.text: Choose one moment to use for now and leave the rest. You do not need to explore every option during a visit.

everyday-comfort-preferences-02.text: You can leave your breathing alone. Try the room based meditation, or simply notice the support beneath you.

everyday-comfort-preferences-05.text: Use a position that is comfortable and safe for you. You do not need to match the illustration.

everyday-comfort-preferences-06.text: You can choose a recording without breathing demonstrations, read the guidance, or pause the audio. Your comfort matters.

everyday-comfort-preferences-07.text: Choose a resting or listening session that suits your position. Adapt the setup to your comfort and access needs.

everyday-comfort-preferences-08.text: A quieter approach is okay. Choose a gentle listening moment and let the next step stay small.

everyday-comfort-preferences-09.text: Your browser or device may offer text size and zoom controls. Use the written guidance at a size that feels comfortable.

everyday-comfort-preferences-10.text: You can return to the appearance choices when you want. A design preference does not need to become a permanent decision.

everyday-clarify-a-need-01.text: Which thing would you like help with? A few ordinary words about the situation are enough to begin.

everyday-clarify-a-need-02.text: Which activity do you mean today? I do not want to choose or change something based on a guess.

everyday-clarify-a-need-05.text: Which time would you like to change, and what should it be instead? The right entry needs to be clear before it is edited.

everyday-clarify-a-need-03.text: What would you like to feel a little easier right now: your next task, your body, or finding a pause?

everyday-clarify-a-need-04.text: Start with what you notice. Are you tired, hungry, restless, overwhelmed, or simply unsure? You can take your time.

everyday-clarify-a-need-08.text: Notice your energy and any discomfort. You could begin with a short pause, then decide whether gentle movement appeals.

everyday-clarify-a-need-06.text: What should the reminder say, and when would later be useful? Check the reminder tool can deliver the notification you need.

everyday-clarify-a-need-07.text: Choose the voice you mean in the unwind session, then use preview or begin. A saved recording cannot identify your previous choice.

everyday-clarify-a-need-09.text: We can leave that idea there. Tell me what you meant in another way, without needing the perfect wording.

everyday-clarify-a-need-10.text: Thanks for correcting that. Choose a sleep or wind down moment so the support fits what you actually wanted.

everyday-several-needs-01.text: Choose what needs attention first, and keep the evening realistic. You can make each part smaller or leave one for another day.

everyday-several-needs-03.text: Tell me your fixed commitments and the time you have. A useful plan needs those details, with some room left open.

everyday-several-needs-04.text: Begin with a brief settling pause. When you are ready, choose one small task instead of the whole list.

everyday-several-needs-02.text: Take care of an immediate ordinary need first if you can. Then reassess how much work reasonably fits the energy left.

everyday-several-needs-06.text: Choose one ending for the scrolling, such as closing the feed. Then take the first small step of getting ready for bed.

everyday-several-needs-05.text: You can choose rest, or a very gentle amount of movement if it suits you. The decision does not need to prove anything.

everyday-several-needs-07.text: Those are two separate app actions. Check the timer is running, then add the food items and verify the list.

everyday-several-needs-08.text: Choose one area for now. Making one ordinary action easier can be enough to begin.

everyday-several-needs-09.text: You can, but it may be easier to let the rest break be a pause first. Check the calendar afterwards if you still want to.

everyday-several-needs-10.text: I can help narrow choices, but your preferences and circumstances still matter. Let's begin with just the next decision.

everyday-real-life-03.text: Use a brief pause when it is safe and practical. Even a small moment of support can fit inside a demanding day.

everyday-real-life-01.text: Let arriving have a little space. Put your things down somewhere safe and settle before asking anything else of yourself.

everyday-real-life-02.text: You do not need complete silence. Find the most comfortable spot available and let the surrounding sounds be part of the moment.

everyday-real-life-05.text: Choose one familiar comfort you can bring into the new place. The rest of the routine can be simpler for now.

everyday-real-life-06.text: Make the next step smaller and include rest where you can. You do not need to use your best day as today's standard.

everyday-real-life-04.text: Build around your own work and rest periods. The clock on someone else's routine does not have to define yours.

everyday-real-life-07.text: Your needs still belong in the day. Consider one practical support you could ask for, alongside a small pause for yourself.

everyday-real-life-08.text: Pause and look at what is still necessary. You can make a new, smaller plan without treating the old one as a failure.

everyday-real-life-09.text: You do not need a special room. A supported seat, a familiar object, or a small comfortable corner can be enough.

everyday-finish-gently-01.text: You can leave it there. Take whatever was useful into the rest of your day.

everyday-finish-gently-02.text: Let that be your next step. There is nothing else you need to finish in the app first.

everyday-real-life-10.text: Then sitting here can be the whole plan. Let yourself arrive without turning the pause into another task.

everyday-finish-gently-04.text: You can pause the audio and stay quietly. The silence does not need filling.

everyday-finish-gently-03.text: That can happen. You have not done it wrong, and you can choose another kind of support or simply move on.

everyday-finish-gently-05.text: Yes. Use end for now whenever you want. You do not need to reach the final second to make the visit worthwhile.

everyday-finish-gently-06.text: That sounds like a practical next step. Let the app wait while you take care of what you need.

everyday-finish-gently-07.text: You can find the session again in Just listen. There is no need to complete another session before returning to it.

everyday-finish-gently-08.text: Use the end conversation control to disconnect live voice. This saved reply cannot close the connection itself.

everyday-finish-gently-09.text: You can visit when you choose. Review any reminders you have set if you no longer want them.

everyday-finish-gently-10.text: Goodnight. Let the remaining tasks wait where they can. You can settle into the rest of your evening at your own pace.
